notes: Scenes are copied from tools/autoflow/act-s1.manifest.json. They are already reviewed against the story file's hard rules, so re-authoring them here would risk losing a rule.
Prompts are English on purpose: image models parse visual description more accurately. No Arabic text is ever rendered inside an image; the story text is a separate layer.
No humans appear in this story, so the catalog hijab / Arab-features clauses do not apply.

Hard rules from the story file, enforced inline in every prompt: nest visible on every page, mother present from page 1, no full darkness, no visible teeth, bird never afraid, 2 characters only, 2-3 elements per page, no burnt-in text.
page-001 is generated FIRST and alone via text-to-image, then reused as a base64 image-to-image reference for every other asset so the bird stays the same character.
PlayVeo returns JPEG, not PNG. The catalog asks for a PNG master, so these outputs are proofs, not final masters, until the provider can emit PNG or a lossless path is added.

PlayVeo accepts explicit ratio strings such as 16:9, 1:1 and 3:4, unlike the AutoFlow Flow models which only expose landscape/portrait/square. That removes the reason act-s1 thumb had to be routed to freepik.

The shared style tail deliberately does NOT fix the sky colour. The catalog's brand palette clause says 'deep space / midnight navy sky', and carrying that into this manifest produced a first attempt at page-001 that came back as a night sky full of stars — directly against the story file, where page 1 is the BRIGHTEST page (brightness 1.00, warm daylight) and a visible moon is mandatory only on the night pages 7 and 8. The brightness curve in the story file outranks the palette default, so light is set per page in the `light` field.

The `light` field carries an explicit negative clause on the daytime pages. Stating the light positively was not enough on the first attempt; the stars only disappeared once 'no stars, no moon' was named.
style_tail: Soft preschool storybook art, rounded shapes, 3 elements max, cyan and star-yellow accents used sparingly, full-bleed to all four edges, no text, no logo, no frame, no border, no visible teeth, no fear.
mode_note: Every asset is text-to-image. The image-to-image endpoint on this provider was tested with six live jobs and returns a byte-identical result for a given source image regardless of the prompt — even 'a bright red sports car in a desert' returned the bird nest, and an explicit strength of 1.0 was echoed back but changed nothing. Padding the file after the JPEG EOI marker did not miss the cache either, so the key is derived from the decoded image, not the bytes. It still bills 0.15 credits per call. Until that is fixed, character identity has to be carried by words, not by a reference image, which is why `character_lock` exists and is prepended to every prompt.
character_lock: Zughb is a tiny round baby bird with very pale light-gray downy feathers, a small soft orange-brown beak, big round dark friendly eyes, soft pink cheek blush, and no teeth ever. His mother is the same pale light-gray but clearly larger, with faint light-brown wing markings and the same big gentle eyes. Only these two birds appear, and they look exactly the same on every page.
character_lock_note: Transcribed from the approved page-001 output so the remaining pages match what was actually generated, rather than describing an intent the model did not follow.
